briefFull: The Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom – Organic Farming: Construction of Vermicompost Units is implemented by the Spices Board, India, under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India.
details: The Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom – Organic Farming: Construction of Vermicompost Units is implemented by the Spices Board, India, under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India. The scheme aims to encourage spice growers to produce vermicompost on their farms by establishing vermicompost units. This helps in the production of high-quality organic manure, improves soil fertility, and promotes the organic cultivation of spices. The scheme is being implemented in accordance with the modalities and guidelines approved by the Competent Authority under the Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom during the 15th Finance Commission period (2021–22 to 2025–26).
benefits:
1. 33.33% of cost one-ton capacity of vermicompost unit @ ₹ 4500/- for Gen and 75% @ ₹ 10,000/- for SC/ST
1. Spices growers having holdings from 0.10 ha to 8.00 ha. A grower having an area upto 4 ha will be eligible to avail a maximum of 1 unit and a grower having area above 4 ha and upto 8 ha will be eligible to avail a maximum of 2 units under the scheme.
1. The size of the vermicompost unit construction will be 2.7 m x 0.9 m x 0.9 m with a capacity to produce one ton in two cycles.
1. Locally available customized units with the above production capacity are also eligible for assistance with supporting bills and documents of purchase and the assistance will be limited to eligible % of assistance of actual cost.
eligibility:
1. All the spice growing States and regions/UTs of India
2. Designated Officials will conduct final inspection and recommend the eligible cases.
3. Preference will be given to farmers who are members of ICS and groups/FPOs
howToApply:
[Online]
**Registration**
Step 1: The applicant should visit the [ServicesPlus](https://serviceonline.gov.in/dbt/) website.
Step 2: Click on the “[Register” ](https://serviceonline.gov.in/dbt/citizenRegistration.html)option on the homepage.
Step 3: Fill out the registration form by entering Full Name, Email ID, Mobile Number, Password, selecting State, and Captcha.
Step 4: Review all details carefully and submit the registration form.
Step 5: An OTP will be sent to your registered mobile number or email; enter the OTP and click “Verify.”
Step 6: Registration will be completed successfully, and a confirmation message will be displayed or sent via email.
**Login**
Step 1: The applicant should visit the ServicesPlus website and click on [“Login.”](https://serviceonline.gov.in/dbt/loginWindow.do)
Step 2: Enter your Email ID, Password, and Captcha.
Step 3: Select the relevant service/scheme name.
Step 4: Fill in the required details in the application form.
Step 5: Submit the application.

faqs.q: What is the objective of the Construction of Vermicompost Unit scheme?
faqs.a: The scheme aims to encourage spice growers to produce vermicompost on their own farms by establishing vermicompost units. This helps improve soil fertility, reduces dependence on chemical fertilizers, and promotes the organic cultivation of spices.

faqs.q: Who can apply for assistance under this scheme?
faqs.a: Spice growers with land holdings ranging from 0.10 hectare to 8.00 hectares are eligible to apply for assistance under the scheme, subject to fulfillment of the prescribed conditions.

faqs.q: What financial assistance is available under the scheme?
faqs.a: General category farmers can receive financial assistance equal to 33.33% of the cost of a one-ton capacity vermicompost unit, subject to a maximum of ₹4,500 per unit. SC/ST farmers are eligible for 75% assistance, subject to a maximum of ₹10,000 per unit.

faqs.q: How many vermicompost units can a farmer receive assistance for?
faqs.a: A grower having land up to 4 hectares is eligible for assistance for a maximum of one vermicompost unit. Growers with land holdings above 4 hectares and up to 8 hectares can receive assistance for a maximum of two units.

faqs.q: What is the standard size of the vermicompost unit?
faqs.a: The standard vermicompost unit should measure 2.7 metres × 0.9 metres × 0.9 metres and should have the capacity to produce one ton of vermicompost in two production cycles.

faqs.q: Are customized vermicompost units eligible for assistance?
faqs.a: Yes. Locally available customized vermicompost units are also eligible for assistance, provided they have the prescribed production capacity and the applicant submits supporting purchase bills and related documents.

faqs.q: Is the subsidy calculated on the actual cost of a customized unit?
faqs.a: Yes. In the case of customized units, assistance is limited to the eligible percentage of the actual cost incurred by the farmer, subject to the maximum assistance allowed under the scheme.

faqs.q: Which documents are required to apply for the scheme?
faqs.a: Applicants are required to submit an Aadhaar Card, the current year's land tax receipt or parcha, and the first page of their bank passbook along with the application.

faqs.q: Is Aadhaar mandatory for availing the benefit?
faqs.a: Yes. Aadhaar is one of the mandatory documents required to establish the identity of the applicant and process the assistance claim.

faqs.q: In which areas is the scheme implemented?
faqs.a: The scheme is available in all spice-growing States, Union Territories, and regions across India where eligible spice cultivation is undertaken.
